structured_output.world_model:
W5 (contrarian), after E051. The tip is E049 at 5.198 s and 0.7535. It is E036 plus an annealed group-2 freeze (LR annealed over 75–90%, frozen for the last 10%) plus a +0.25-epoch top-up, for about 238 steps. E050 rebuilt the same commit and read 0.7552 at 5.206 s. I missed on time because I had anchored to E036. The population mean on seeds 0–2 is about 0.754, and time reproduces to about ±0.02 s.

1. Noise. Rebuilds of one commit spread with an SD of about 0.2 pp on the 3-seed mean (E036: 0.7532/0.7525/0.7497/0.7544; E049: 0.7535/0.7552). Any change that costs ≥0.1 pp is close to a coin flip at the 0.753 gate. Forecast bands need about ±0.3 pp.

2. Weight decay acts only through the SGD groups, because Muon renormalizes the filters and applies no wd. The optimum is near ×0.5.

3. Annealed freezes are the best lever found. Freezing a block skips its memory-bound BN/GELU backward, its Muon NS, the dgrad into it and the optimizer traffic, so it saves 1.5–2× the block's FLOP share (E028, E046: about 10 ms per frozen step). Accuracy holds when the anneal is gentle and the block has trained at 32 px. Starting earlier costs roughly in proportion and then hits a cliff (E037). My E046 miss: I underestimated both the time saving and the accuracy neutrality. Group 2 tolerates a short tail freeze. Extending the dose (I082) should still trade at or slightly better than the dial, but the anneal window shrinks toward the 70% resolution switch, where the E037-like cliff risk lives.

4. Steps carry accuracy; early pixels do not. E026 and E033 were free. Removing steps or samples (E031, E040, E041, E048) costs about the dial rate, 1.2–1.8 s/pp. Selection plus a top-up should therefore net about zero, minus the topk/scatter overhead.

5. "How training ends" is at a tuned local optimum. Every booster that touched the averaging, the loss or BN recalibration lost 0.2–0.5 pp (E025, E030, E032, E044).

6. Stem architecture. E051 confirmed my prior: the strided conv was −0.29 s and −0.9 pp, about 0.3 s/pp, much worse than the dial. Max-pool invariance matters on CIFAR-100. ReLU in place of GELU: the fused kernels are bytes-bound. Inductor's saved tensors for ReLU (a bool mask, or the fp16 output) cut backward reads only partly, so I expect about a 1.5–3% gain. The accuracy loss should be 0.2–0.4 pp, because GELU's gain in airbench was real and CIFAR-100 is more sensitive. That is worse than the dial.

7. Still unexploited, with identical math: (a) lazy per-epoch augmentation. The final epoch loop augments, interpolates and permutes the full 50k for about 13 steps. (b) Skip the Lookahead foreach lerp/copy over frozen params after their freeze point. Frozen fast weights equal the EMA up to the lerp, so the math changes only negligibly. Together these are worth about 1–2%. They are the safest remaining gains, and nobody has run them.

8. Transfer to the PCIe judge: absolute times should come in 5–10% higher, and the ranking should hold. The bigger risk is that the true population mean is about 0.753–0.754. That is thin headroom over the official 0.75 bar, but it is acceptable.

Unsure:
- whether rebuild variance comes from autotune or from atomics (E050 arm results unreported);
- whether seeds 13–32 are harder or the gap is winner's curse;
- whether a 70%-start group-2 anneal crosses a cliff.

forecasts.reason: The fused BN/activation kernels are bytes-bound, so ReLU saves only about 2%. GELU is worth about 0.2–0.4 pp on short CIFAR-100 runs, so the rate is worse than the dial.
Selection trades at about the dial rate (E031, E048). A net cut of about 5 steps saves about 0.1 s and costs about 0.1 pp, which is inside the noise.

About 13 more frozen steps at about 10 ms each save about 0.13 s. But the anneal now starts at the 32 px switch, so the 32 px training of group 2 is cut short, an E037-like risk. Expect −0.1 to −0.3 pp.

cruxes: Is there an accuracy cliff when group 2's anneal starts at the 70% resolution switch (I082), as there was for the stem in E037? This decides whether the freeze cascade can keep scaling.

How much of the remaining time is outside the step graphs: the full-dataset augmentation, interpolation and permute in the final partial epoch, and the Lookahead traffic over frozen params? Cutting these keeps the math identical and costs no accuracy.
Is the tip's build-to-build spread of about 0.2 pp reducible (E050 arms 1–3)? If not, every gain under 0.15 pp is unmeasurable and only time levers with identical math are worth running.
